instructions: Drain the lentils in a strainer and rinse them under cold water. Mince the garlic and dice the onion.
Heat the 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 tsp salt. Cook, stirring now and then, for 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp chili powder and 1/2 tsp cumin. Stir for 1 minute, until it smells toasty.
Add the 3 tbsp tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until it darkens a shade.
In a small bowl, stir together the 2 tbsp ketchup, 1 tbsp maple syrup, 2 tsp vinegar, 1 tbsp soy sauce and 3/4 cup water. Pour it into the skillet and scrape up anything stuck to the bottom.

Add the lentils and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt. Simmer over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often. Press some of the lentils against the side of the pan with the back of a spoon as you go. It's ready when most of the liquid is gone and it holds together on the spoon.
While it simmers, toast the buns cut side down in a dry skillet or in the toaster until golden, about 2 minutes.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spoon the lentils onto the bottom buns, top with the pickle slices and close the sandwiches. Serve with the hot sauce on the side.
method_notes: No version of this dish has 20 or more ratings, so this is a fallback lead: I Heart Vegetables' Vegan Lentil Sloppy Joes (4.4 from 5), with Vegan with Gusto's version (5.0 from 1) read as a second. Both simmer dried green lentils for 25 to 40 minutes, so canned lentils replace them to land under 30 minutes; the sauce and spices follow the lead. Adapted to stay vegan: soy sauce and vinegar instead of Worcestershire, maple syrup for sweetness, and vegan buns. Pickles and the hot sauce on the side are additions for crunch and heat.
